title: The fourth week

lines: SHE TAKES HIM FOR THE GARDENER.
cards: A woman is crying outside a tomb in the early morning. The body she came to care for is gone. Someone is standing behind her, and she takes him for the gardener.
She asks him, if he has carried the body away, to tell her where. He doesn't give her a speech about the resurrection. He doesn't show her proof.
He says one word, and it's her name. That's enough. The fourth week of the Exercises is full of moments like this, and Ignatius has a title for what Christ is doing in each.

teach.b: The fourth week turns from the tomb to the risen Christ. Yesterday, the divinity hid itself in the passion. Now, Ignatius says, it shows itself, in the resurrection and in what it does.
He asks the one praying to watch for one thing in every appearance: the office of consoler. Office, as in a job.
Christ carries out the work of consoling, and Ignatius says to compare it with the way friends console one another.
Mary Magdalene at the tomb, in the Douay-Rheims: "Jesus saith to her: Mary. She turning, saith to him: Rabboni."
Two disciples on the road to Emmaus, sad and confused, and he walks beside them, talking, a long way before they know who he is.

teach.h: A NAME, A WALK, A BREAKFAST.
teach.b: Peter, who had denied him, is given breakfast on the beach. Each is consoled in a way that fits them. Ignatius begins the week somewhere surprising: with an appearance to Our Lady, his mother.
He admits scripture doesn't mention it, and says it should be understood all the same, since scripture tells of him appearing to so many others.
The grace to ask for changes too: not sorrow now, but to be glad and rejoice in Christ's joy.
His joy, not only mine. Even the outward helps change: in this week Ignatius suggests light, fresh air, and thinking of things that bring joy.

how: In the fourth week of an Ignatian retreat, people contemplate the appearances of the risen Christ, asking for the grace to rejoice in his joy and noticing how he consoles each person he meets.

games.q: you're Mary Magdalene, weeping at the empty tomb. a man you take for the gardener is standing behind you. what makes you recognize him?
o: he shows you the empty grave.
games.why: "Mary." one word, her name, and she turns and says "Rabboni." Ignatius would call it the office of consoler at work.

practice: Look back over the last week for one moment of consolation, in Ignatius's sense: a kind word, a sky, a laugh you didn't expect, a peace that came out of nowhere.
Let it play again, notice who brought it or how it arrived, and stay with the gladness without hurrying past. If you pray, thank Christ for it; if you don't, let the good of it land.

wordCard.voice: The fourth week. The risen Christ as consoler, meeting each person in the way that fits them. This week ran from the call of the king, through the two standards and the art of choosing, to the passion and the resurrection. Today's word.

orig.note: Spanish, the language Ignatius wrote in: to console. he speaks of the office of consoling that Christ carries out.

carryVoice: Your line: the consoler. Not with arguments: with a name, a walk, a meal. That's today, done.
